_comment: Source of truth for the brand-image shortlist. Hand-edit this file, then run ./tools/images-sync.py. Rank is the ORDER within a category — move an entry up to promote it, delete it to drop it. Rebuilt 2026-08-07 as five visual families, one coherent photographic world: candid over posed, environmental portraits over headshots, humans using technology over technology alone.

adobe.name: Adobe Stock
adobe.licence: Watermarked comp. Evaluation only until licensed.
adobe.note: Standard subscription. Premium collections (Stocksy, Westend61, peopleimages) are resold here but cost extra.

unsplash.name: Unsplash
unsplash.licence: Unsplash Licence — free for commercial use, no attribution required.
unsplash.note: Free and heavily used, so exclusivity is nil: the same photo can appear on a competitor's site. Good for internal decks and filler; check every frame for third-party logos, which Unsplash does not screen out the way paid libraries do.

envato.name: Envato Elements
envato.licence: Covered by the RBA subscription — licensed on download, usable in production.
envato.note: The only source here that is actually licensed. Previews staged by tools/images-fetch-envato.py are watermarked 1200x630 social crops; download the clean full-size file over the same filename and the watermark goes.

istock.name: iStock
istock.licence: Not licensed. Credit or subscription required before use.
istock.note: Getty's affordable tier. Signature collection is exclusive to Getty/iStock, so it is not resold through Adobe — that is the reason to have it here rather than a price one.

items.title: Diverse coworkers collaborating on open laptop in bright office near windows, woman wearing tan top
items.why: Two colleagues actually reading the same screen, with expressions that belong to the work rather than the camera. Big windows, business casual, no staging.
items.crop: 3:2 as shot; keep both faces and the laptop lid.

items.title: I have some ideas for you. Shot of a group of businesspeople having a meeting at work.
items.why: A working session that looks mid-sentence: one person talking, five actually listening, whiteboard scrawl behind. The warm daylight keeps it human.
items.crop: Wide 2:1; crop toward the speaker for cards.

items.title: Two Professionals Review Business Contract Together Before Signing
items.why: Consultant and client at real monitors, one pointing at actual work on screen. Reads as a review, not a photoshoot.
items.crop: Keep both screens; wide crops hold.

items.title: Businesswoman holding digital tablet near whiteboard in meeting
items.why: A whiteboard dense with real writing and a presenter mid-thought. Documentary register that most whiteboard stock never reaches.
items.crop: Keep the whiteboard texture; faces are secondary here.

items.title: Three colleagues around a laptop with printed charts across the desk, one leaning in over the others
items.why: A desk with a project actually on it — printouts, notebooks, a laptop three people are reading. Everyone is looking at the work rather than past it, which the frame it replaces could not manage.
items.use: Project delivery, team pages, staff augmentation
items.crop: 3:2; keep the printouts in the foreground and the windows behind.

items.title: Creative brainstorming session strategy photo
items.why: A strategist reading a wall of notes and wireframes, tablet in hand. Process made visible without a single sticky-note cliche pose.
items.crop: Portraitish subject; leave wall texture around her.

items.title: Two colleagues standing in discussion beside a glass wall covered in sticky notes, one holding an open folder
items.why: A standing working conversation with the workshop still on the glass behind it. Gestures and folder do the talking, so it reads as discovery rather than a corridor walk-and-talk.
items.crop: Keep the sticky-note wall in frame; crops to 4:3 without losing either face.

items.title: Group Strategizing Collaboratively, Collaborative Team Reviewing Project Timelines And Presentation Charts
items.why: A team reading one timeline together, bottles and laptops where a real meeting leaves them. The panorama is a gift for banners.
items.crop: Native 2.1:1 panorama; ideal under a light overlay.

items.title: Two happy diverse multiethnic business team people working, talking in corporate office
items.why: A one-on-one at the window that is clearly a working conversation, not a coffee ad. Genuine expressions, believable office.
items.crop: 3:2; keep the window light on both faces.

items.title: Focused on achieving her career goals. Cropped shot of an attractive young businesswoman working at her desk
items.why: Tight crop on real concentration, screen light on the face. The rare close portrait that is about the work, not the smile.
items.crop: Already cropped tight; use at card size or half-width.

items.title: Designer at an iMac in profile, absorbed in the layout on screen, daylight and a plant behind
items.why: A face doing the work, which the frame it replaces did not have — that one was hands over a desk of props. Design shown as concentration rather than as a spread of printed screens.
items.use: UX practice, design services, case studies
items.crop: 3:2; keep the screen content and the window light on his face.

items.title: IT technician in startup office using large language model to get help with coding project
items.why: A developer at a multi-monitor rig in a brick-walled studio, colleague passing behind. Warm, credible, and specifically technical.
items.crop: Wide; keep at least two screens legible.

items.title: Analyst at a three-monitor desk reaching to a chart on screen in a window-lit office
items.why: Real spreadsheets and real charts across three screens, and a hand reaching into the work. Daylight from the window keeps it out of the blue-glow register the category kept falling into.
items.crop: 3:2; keep at least two screens and the window edge.

items.title: Designer leaning over a notebook mid-sentence, contact sheets spread across the desk in a concrete loft office
items.why: Real concentration, caught from the side rather than presented to camera. The prints and the notebook are the work, not props arranged around it. Replaces a white-box frame that was lit like a catalogue and posed like one.
items.use: Craft and method, design and research, individual expertise
items.crop: 3:2. Keep the spread of prints along the bottom edge; do not crop to a head-and-shoulders.

items.title: Young businesswoman thinking about something while sitting front open portable laptop computer
items.why: Caught mid-thought behind foreground foliage, one hand to the chin. Editorial texture most workstation stock lacks.
items.crop: Keep the foreground blur; do not crop square.

items.title: Portrait of confident senior woman manager using laptop computer working online sitting in modern office
items.why: A senior manager actually working: laptop, notebook, warm slatted light. Experience without the arms-folded executive pose.
items.crop: 3:2; the blinds pattern rewards a wide crop.

items.title: Woman graphic designer working at dual monitors in modern office
items.why: Dual monitors, a desk fan, cable clutter: a workstation that is clearly used daily. She turns from the work, not for the camera.
items.crop: Keep both monitors and the room depth.

items.title: A young woman in a white shirt uses a tablet in a modern office setting with large windows and natural light
items.why: Reading on a tablet, standing at the glass. Quiet, bright, and free of the usual tablet-as-prop stiffness.
items.use: Mobile workflows, reading lists, secondary pages
items.crop: Vertical-friendly; also crops to 3:2.

items.title: Colleague gesturing at a dashboard on a desktop monitor while the other follows with a pen
items.why: A readout in progress, shot over the listener's shoulder so the viewer sits in the client's chair. The dashboard is a real one and the frame is bright — the hero the category deserved.
items.crop: Keep the screen legible; the over-shoulder foreground is the composition.

items.title: Woman Working At Office Desk, Using Online Banking App
items.why: A real application on real screens, one finger on the data. Human use of software with zero sci-fi garnish.
items.use: Applied AI, digital products, service pages
items.crop: Wide 1.9:1; screen stays legible at banner size.

items.title: Colleague at a wall screen walking a seated coworker through a spreadsheet, daylight and plants
items.why: An actual spreadsheet on the screen and a working room around it: wood table, window, someone listening. Replaces a huddle that read as three people arguing in a startup.
items.crop: 3:2; the screen has to stay legible — it is the reason the picture works.

items.title: Woman programmer works at desk in modern loft office coding on large monitors with natural light and brick wall
items.why: Code on a big monitor, brick and daylight around it. Engineering that looks like a place you would want to work.
items.crop: 3:2; window flare is part of the appeal.

items.title: A professional group of Asian business colleagues having a meeting in a bright modern office
items.why: Laptops on the table, charts on the wall screen, a standing presenter mid-point. A workshop, not a keynote.
items.crop: Keep table laptops and wall screen in one frame.

items.title: Data scientists working together in server room, reviewing neural network code and LLM visualization dashboards
items.why: Two data scientists reading a laptop inside a server aisle. Bridges data work and infrastructure without a glowing cloud in sight.
items.use: Cloud and data platform, MLOps, infrastructure
items.crop: Keep the aisle depth behind them.

items.title: Professional Asian business team gathering around desk to analyze data on laptop screen
items.why: Four heads bent over one laptop, hands on the desk. Process discussion with real body language.
items.crop: 3:2; crop keeps all four faces.

items.title: Business colleagues reviewing data on tablet at cafe
items.why: A tablet passed across a cafe table between three colleagues. The device sits inside a genuine conversation.
items.crop: Warm tones; crops to square for cards.

items.title: A briefing under way in a glass-walled room, dashboard on the wall screen, seen from the floor outside
items.why: Observed through the glass rather than staged inside it, so it reads as a meeting that was already happening. Daylight, ordinary clothes, a dashboard nobody is pointing at — the opposite of the neon control room it replaces.
items.crop: 3:2; keep the glass line and the screen. Do not crop into the room.

items.title: A team of three colleagues intently reviews market share statistics displayed on a large screen
items.why: Three colleagues against a wall of charts and boards, two pointing at different things. Complex information being genuinely argued over.
items.crop: Keep the full stat wall behind the trio.

items.title: Female industrial engineer inspecting manufacturing equipment using digital tablet inside modern production facility
items.why: An engineer with a tablet inspecting equipment, shallow focus keeping her the subject. The person outranks the machinery, as the brief asks.
items.use: Manufacturing industry page, IoT, field work
items.crop: 3:2; machinery bokeh should stay soft.

items.title: Hospital, meeting and doctor with team on tablet for report, patient results and treatment plan
items.why: A doctor mid-explanation, tablet in hand, colleagues leaning in. Clinical teamwork with believable energy.
items.crop: 16:9 native; keep all three faces.

items.title: Man in a business shirt checking stock on a tablet in a bright retail aisle
items.why: One person, a device, a real aisle going soft behind — the exact grammar rbaconsulting.com uses for its own photography, and the sharpest retail frame in the set.
items.use: Retail industry page, inventory and store operations
items.crop: 3:2; keep the aisle receding behind him for depth.

items.title: Engineering team reviews maintenance data on laptop during equipment inspection inside manufacturing facility
items.why: Two engineers with a laptop at the machine they are actually discussing. Equipment context without anyone posing on it.
items.crop: Keep the machine's green mass in frame.

items.title: Diverse medical team collaborating around a table, discussing healthcare strategies and using laptops
items.why: A clinical team around a table with laptops, glass wall behind. The administrative half of healthcare that photo libraries forget.
items.crop: Wide; crop to the table for cards.

items.title: Engineer in a blazer reading a tablet beside a robotic arm on a bright factory floor
items.why: Automation photographed the way rbaconsulting.com photographs industry: business casual, no hard hat, no hi-vis, one person absorbed in a device with the plant soft behind her. The PPE frame it replaces was the furthest thing here from that.
items.crop: 3:2; keep the arm in the foreground blur and her face lit.

items.title: Business Meeting Between Two Professionals Reviewing Documents on a Tablet in Modern Office Lounge
items.why: Advisor and client on a lounge sofa over one tablet. Financial services warmth without a handshake in sight.
items.crop: 3:2; the sofa's warm palette crops well.

items.title: Young professional IT specialist business lady working on laptop sitting at desk in modern office space
items.why: A banking professional at her laptop behind the glass partition, half-smile aimed at the work. Clean, credible, unposed.
items.crop: Keep the glass reflection layer.

items.title: Warehouse worker and factory manager using a digital tablet to check barcodes and inspect stock inventory
items.why: An operations manager with a tablet dwarfed by warehouse racking. Scale and the person, in one frame.
items.crop: Vertical racking rewards a tall crop too.

items.title: Plant manager with a tablet on a food production floor, sorting line and crew soft behind her
items.why: Keeps the food and agriculture subject this slot deliberately holds, but photographs it the way the rest of the library photographs industry: one person, a device, business dress rather than costume, the operation going on behind her. The frame it replaces was a plaid shirt and a bucket hat in a field, which reads as agriculture stock rather than a client.
items.use: Food and agriculture, manufacturing operations, supply chain
items.crop: Wide 16:9. Keep the line running to the left; she sits on the right third with room for a headline over the conveyor.

items.title: Two businessmen discussing at an outdoor cafe in the city
items.why: Two colleagues deep in conversation at an outdoor cafe, warm brick behind, shot over a shoulder. The city register the rest of the family keeps.
items.crop: 3:2; keep the foreground shoulder, it frames the scene.

items.title: Business colleagues having a discussion while walking past modern office buildings in the city
items.why: Three colleagues crossing at the light between glass towers, mid-conversation. The commute as connective tissue.
items.crop: 3:2; keep the crossing stripes underfoot.

items.title: Volunteers planting trees in a sunny park
items.why: A wide, sunlit frame of volunteers actually planting, nobody aware of the camera. Community work photographed as work, in the documentary register.
items.crop: Wide 3:2; the depth of the park matters, do not crop tight.

items.title: Diverse women colleagues enjoying lunch break together
items.why: Takeout boxes, mid-sentence gestures, actual lunch. The team meal without the pizza-box grin.
items.crop: 3:2; warm tones hold in tight crops.

items.title: Colleagues gathered on a rooftop terrace over the city
items.why: A rooftop table over the city at dusk, string lights up, nobody performing. The informal-social concept where this family lives, outdoors.
items.crop: Wide; the skyline band takes overlay copy.

items.title: Three colleagues talking on outdoor stairs beside a modern building, coffee in hand, low sun behind
items.why: Genuinely mixed ages in a conversation that is clearly already happening — one arriving up the steps, two mid-exchange. Replaces four people seated in a row on a wall, which read as a casting sheet rather than a break.
items.use: Culture, careers, hybrid and flexible working, About
items.crop: Very wide as shot, which suits a banner. Keep all three and the stair rail; the left third is empty enough for type.

items.title: Woman working on a laptop on a sofa in a daylit living room with tall windows
items.why: Wide enough to be about the room, not the laptop. Bright, calm and ungraded, with space at the left for a headline — hybrid work photographed as a life rather than a setup.
items.crop: Wide 3:2; the left third is empty on purpose, so keep it.

items.title: Three diverse women laughing with coffee on a city street
items.why: A genuine laugh between three colleagues mid-stride, coffee in hand, on a real street. Humor kept, moved into daylight and the city.
items.crop: 3:2; keep all three faces and the street depth.

items.title: This is our time to catch up. Shot of two young businessmen walking through the city during their afternoon commute
items.why: Two professionals walking the sunny street, one wheeling a bike. Commute-as-lifestyle with real ease between them.
items.crop: Wide 1.85:1; open sky takes type.

items.title: Diverse coworkers collaborating and talking in a modern office, enjoying a casual break with natural light and plants
items.why: A standing group mid-conversation by the windows, framed through plants. An inclusive group photo that never squares up to the camera.
items.crop: 3:2; keep the foreground greenery.

items.title: Developer at a three-screen workstation with real code open, daylight across a wooden floor
items.why: Actual code on actual screens, headphones over the chair, daylight doing the work. Everything the composited neon-code frame it replaces was pretending to be.
items.crop: 3:2; keep all three displays and the room behind.

items.title: Laptop workspace with coffee cup and small cactus on wooden table near bright window
items.why: The real-workplace register from the guideline — daylight, plant, no people, believable desk. Warm counterweight to the abstracts.
items.use: Culture and flexible-work content, blog headers
items.crop: 3:2 as shot; keep window light on the left.

items.title: Computer monitors displaying source code in a modern workstation with laptop
items.why: A working development environment shown plainly — screens with real code, no neon grading, no hoodie theater.
items.crop: 3:2 centered on the primary monitor.

items.title: Low angle view of a modern open-plan office conference table with laptops and natural light
items.why: The workplace wide shot: laptops, mugs, daylight, nobody posing. Sets scene without staging one.
items.crop: 3:2 as shot; the table line anchors the lower third.

items.title: Video conference meeting on a laptop screen, close up, teleconference collaboration at home
items.why: Distributed collaboration as it actually looks — a laptop grid of faces in a living room. Matches the guideline's fourth example.
items.crop: 3:2 on the screen; keep a sliver of the room for context.

items.title: Two colleagues at one laptop, one holding a printout, working through it together in a bright office
items.why: Someone being shown something — which is what onboarding and internal comms actually look like. Warm daylight, plants, both people in the task rather than posed beside it.
items.crop: 3:2; keep both faces and the printed page.

items.title: Pale particle wave drifting across a white field, dots thickening to blue at the crest
items.why: The one background here that works on a white page. A wave made of dots, nearly all of it empty, blue only where the particles bunch. Nothing to fight a headline and nothing to date it.
items.use: Section dividers, light-mode headers, deck title slides, quote plates
items.crop: Vector, so crop to any ratio. Crop off the bottom-right corner — the artwork carries the words "ABSTRACT BACKGROUND" there.

items.title: Blue contour lines rippling across a deep navy field, concentric rings at the peak
items.why: Line work on the brand navy, and the left third is almost empty — the rare data-flow graphic with somewhere to put type. No numbers, no binary, no baked-in words.
items.use: Full-bleed headers, data and analytics pages, dark-mode heroes
items.crop: 16:9 as shot. Set type in the dark left third; do not crop into the rings.

items.title: Minimalist plexus of white and silver dots connected by fine beams over a blue-to-black gradient
items.why: The quietest network graphic found — silver on deep blue with built-in copy space. For when the orange-accent plexus is too loud.
items.crop: 16:9 native; the center is deliberately empty for type.

items.title: Abstract digital network with glowing blue and orange connection lines and dots
items.why: The network abstract from the brand guideline's own Technology examples — navy field, warm accent nodes, restrained glow.
items.use: Data and connectivity sections, dark deck backgrounds
items.crop: Panoramic; crop to the densest cluster for 3:2.

items.title: White structural members crossing a deep blue sky, seen from directly below
items.why: Structure and sky reduced to three shapes. The blue is the brand's own and the white cuts across it hard enough to carry reversed type — ambition without the business-district cliché the previous frame fell into.
items.use: Vision and strategy pages, hero bands, presentations
items.crop: 3:2 or wider; keep the sky quadrant clear for type.

items.title: Dotted data grid on a dark surface receding into shallow focus, amber and cyan blocks
items.why: Shallow depth of field does the work a flat vector cannot: it reads as a surface photographed rather than a diagram drawn. Navy with amber accents, which is close to the palette without being forced there.
items.use: Platform and engineering pages, data infrastructure, section headers
items.crop: 16:9. The blurred top band is the quiet area; keep type out of the sharp centre.

items.title: Streaming rows of code and data receding to a bright vanishing point, warm bokeh at the left
items.why: Depth and motion in one frame, with warm out-of-focus lights keeping the blue from going cold. Disclosed on Adobe as Generative AI — the licensing check on this page says confirm that before buying.
items.use: Dark-mode headers, engineering and cloud topics, event backdrops
items.crop: Crop toward the left half, where the bokeh is soft enough to hold reversed type.

items.title: Bundles of abstract optical fiber lines carrying light signals
items.why: Infrastructure made visual — flowing strands, blue-white light, motion without blur clichés.
items.crop: 3:2 from the left two-thirds where the strands converge.

items.title: Facade of repeating triangular glass panels
items.why: A triangulated facade that reads as a network without a glowing node in sight. Connectivity, drawn by a building.
items.use: Connectivity and platform stories, section breaks
items.crop: Pattern fills any frame; avoid cropping to featurelessness.

items.title: Green and blue waveform rising across a dark field with plotted markers and rule lines
items.why: Analytics drawn as a signal rather than a network. Note the green: it is off-palette, so this is the one to reach for last, or to recolour at the vector level if the licence allows.
items.use: Analytics and measurement pages, performance topics
items.crop: Crop from the left, where the waveform flattens and the field is nearly empty.

items.title: Layered red and teal data threads peaking across a navy grid, numbers plotted along the curves
items.why: The busiest frame in this family and the most literal — a chart made ornamental. It earns a place as a texture, not as a plate for type.
items.use: Small crops, card backgrounds, texture behind a solid panel
items.crop: Do not run type over this uncropped. Take a quiet corner, or lay a solid panel over it.

items.title: The vein network of a backlit leaf, close up
items.why: A leaf lit until its veins read as a network. The one connectivity metaphor here drawn from nature rather than neon.
items.use: Data and connectivity stories, sustainability-adjacent pages
items.crop: Veins hold detail in tight crops.
